rules.replace: she smiles at the camera, waves hello with her right hand, then turns her head to look along the park path, laughs, and looks back at the camera with a happy smile
The camera slowly moves a little closer to her, staying at chest height
Birdsong, leaves rustling in a light breeze and the soft sounds of a quiet park. No speech, no voice.
A light, happy acoustic guitar tune with soft hand claps and a gentle shaker, at a relaxed tempo.

promptState.text:
subject_definitions:
<Picture 1> is the first frame and composition anchor for [Shot 1], defining the complete visible image exactly as supplied, including the framing, camera viewpoint, subject placement, subject scale, crop, foreground-to-background relationship, whatever forms the area behind and around the subject, lighting, shadows, colors, gradients, depth cues, and overall scene composition. Its rendering style, whether photographic, illustrated, stylised, or three-dimensional, is part of what is preserved.
<Subject 1> is the main visible figure defined by <Picture 1>, preserved exactly as it appears there. Whatever <Subject 1> already is remains unchanged: its form, proportions, head shape, facial structure, surface, colors, markings, and every visible garment, covering, accessory, and detail. Nothing is added that is not already visible in <Picture 1>, and nothing visible is removed, replaced, simplified, or reinterpreted.
<Subject 2> is the complete visible area behind, beneath, beside, and around <Subject 1> as defined by <Picture 1>, preserving its exact colors, surfaces, objects if any are present, spatial layout, lighting, shadows, gradients, and depth. Whatever that area looks like in <Picture 1> is exactly what it looks like in the target video, including its overall tone and brightness, and it is never exchanged for a different kind of surrounding. If objects are present, exactly those objects remain, and no further ones appear.

summary:
[keyframe completion] The target video begins from <Picture 1> and animates <Subject 1> in one continuous shot, preserving the exact appearance of <Subject 1> and the complete visible area represented by <Subject 2>.

retention_analysis:
<Picture 1> ([Shot 1] first frame): fully_preserved - the supplied image is the starting frame, retaining its viewpoint, framing, subject placement, surroundings, lighting, and rendering style.
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the appearance shown in the reference remains intact in every visible respect, with natural movement permitted.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the referenced surroundings remain visually identical, with nothing substituted, added, or removed.

detailed_description:
The target video develops directly from the complete supplied image in <Picture 1>, preserving its rendering style, color treatment, lighting, composition, and full visible scene. <Picture 1> is the actual starting frame, not merely an appearance reference for the foreground.
[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1>. [CAMERA]. <Subject 1> keeps the exact appearance established in <Picture 1> in every visible respect, and no feature, marking, covering, or accessory is introduced that is not already present there. <Subject 2> keeps the complete visible area exactly as referenced, including its colors, surfaces, shadows, lighting direction, and depth. <Subject 1> is never lifted out of the supplied scene and placed into a newly generated one, and the surroundings are never exchanged for a different setting. In the video, [ACTION]. The face, hair, body and clothing of <Subject 1> stay consistent in every frame, and the movement is smooth and natural. Flexible details such as hair and loose clothing show natural secondary motion.

overall_soundscape:
[SOUND]

non_diegetic_music:
[MUSIC]

{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Your picture becomes a video that does what you write: what the person does, how the camera moves, the sounds and the music. The picture is the first frame, so the place, the light and the person stay.

 Steps

  1. 1. Pick how many seconds.
  2. 2. Load your picture.
  3. 3. Leave the video size at 864 to start.
  4. 4. In Find and Replace, fill the four boxes (see below).
  5. 5. Seed: F (fixed) or R (random).
  6. Press Run.

 The four boxes

  • [ACTION]: what happens, in order, in plain words: she smiles at the camera, waves hello with her right hand, then turns her head to look along the park path, laughs, and looks back at the camera.
  • [CAMERA]: one move, or none: The camera slowly moves a little closer to her, or The camera stays still.
  • [SOUND]: what you hear in the place. End with No speech, no voice when nobody should talk.
  • [MUSIC]: H3 makes the music from your sentence: the instruments, the mood and the tempo. Write N/A for no music, the way the trained prompt marks an empty part.

 Good to know

  • In the tests (4 seeds) she did every action in order, and H3 made the music on all 4 with no speech.
  • Keep the person close: from the knees up or closer. A person far away in the picture gets small in the video and loses detail.
  • Letters on clothes, like PIXA on her t-shirt, stayed readable even while she turned.
  • Another seed gives another take.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Nodes look different from the video 

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"How to Use","icon":"to-do","color":"#2a9d8f"}}

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (MiniMax H3 ref2va) - MiniMax H3, the video model. This is its Reference to Video version: besides your prompt it can look at pictures and at a video you give it.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL, reads prompt and pictures) - Qwen3-VL 32B: reads your prompt and looks at your picture.
  • Load VAE (video) - Turns the finished render into video frames, and your video into the model's own format.
  • Load VAE (sound) - Turns sound into the model's format and back.
  • LoRA Loader Pixaroma (speed) - Holds the DMAD 4-step speed LoRA: 4 steps instead of 20, same look.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Duration Pixaroma (1. how many seconds) - How many seconds the video lasts, turned into the frame count H3 accepts.
  • Load Image Mini Pixaroma (2. your picture, the first frame) - Your picture. It becomes the FIRST FRAME of the video, so the place, the light and the person stay. From the knees up or closer keeps the face and details sharp.
  • Longest Side Pixaroma (3. video size) - The size of the video by its longest side; your picture keeps its shape. 864 is the default and fast; 1024 and 1280 are sharper but slower. The step is 32 because H3 needs sizes that are multiples of 32.
  • Find and Replace Pixaroma (4. what happens, the camera, the sound, the music) - Four short boxes that fill the [ACTION], [CAMERA], [SOUND] and [MUSIC] places of the prompt below. This is where you tell the video what to do.
  • Prompt Pixaroma (the prompt, leave it) - The trained prompt. It tells H3 that your picture is the first frame and that the person, the place and the light must stay; your boxes go into its empty places. Leave it as it is.
  • Seed Pixaroma (5. random or fixed) - The seed. F (fixed) gives the same result every Run, R (random) a new one each Run.

 Working in the background

Teal. They run by themselves: they make the steps faster, hand memory back, lock the real sound into the render or guide the moves. The line next to each one says if there is anything worth changing.

  • MiniMaxH3SigmaShift (12 / 3 for the speed LoRA) - The noise schedule for the speed LoRA: 12 for the picture, 3 for the sound. Leave it as it is.
  • Model Attention Backend (faster steps) - Picks the attention maths. comfy kitchen attention makes each step about 1.7 times faster on NVIDIA and AMD cards with the same look (measured). If you get an error with it, pick pytorch attention.
  • Free VRAM Pixaroma (before the decode) - Hands the graphics card's memory back between the render and the video decode, so the decode fits on smaller cards.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo (prompt + your picture) - Builds the empty video at your size and length and reads the prompt together with your picture (<Picture 1>).
  • ConditioningZeroOut (empty negative) - An empty negative prompt. H3 runs at CFG 1 here, where the negative does nothing, but the KSampler still needs one plugged in.
  • KSampler (4 steps) - The render: 4 steps, CFG 1, euler, simple, the settings the speed LoRA is made for.
  • VAE Decode (render to video frames) - Turns the finished render into video frames.
  • VAE Decode Audio (the sound and music) - Turns the sound H3 made, the place and the music, into audio for the saved video.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Video Pixaroma (the video) - Saves the video as MP4 into ComfyUI/output/Picture Videos with the sound and music H3 made, and plays it on the node.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Nodes Info","icon":"node-v5","color":"#3d7cc9"}}

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the time grows with the size and with the seconds.

Video size5 seconds
864 (480 x 864), the defaultabout 18 to 22 s

Times are with comfy kitchen attention (the default here). With pytorch attention the render part takes about 1.7 times as long.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models (about 20 GB for H3 and 15 GB for its text encoder), so it takes longer. After that they stay loaded.

 On a smaller card

Start with the smallest size and 5 seconds. The Free VRAM node already hands memory back before the video decode. A clip that is too big for the card gets very slow long before it stops working.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
